applies_why: The judge text weighs the challenger's own multi-verse chain against the defender's chain at a link, which is the chain-against-chain collision the rule governs.
quote: the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse
room: The phrase 'does not name Joseph as the begetter' could be read either as a verse-by-verse absence-of-statement objection the rule forbids, or as a footing observation about what the chain's footing supports; I read it as the latter because the sentence weighs both chains by their footing.
why: The judge sets the two chains against each other by their footing and does not reject the challenger's chain merely because no single verse states the contrary.
